items.summary: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models. items.summary: Video foresight reasoning requires vision-language models to anticipate future events or next actions from currently observed videos. items.summary: We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation. items.title: Duopra: From Full-Duplex Conversation to Full-Duplex Agency
items.summary: Full-duplex interaction models exhibit strong conversational agency, enabling natural, low-latency turn-taking, backchannels, and interruptions. items.title: Plan4D: Generative Plannable 4D Worlds
items.summary: Most world models for future prediction prioritize aestetic quality of generated videos, but offer only weak physical grounding and limited geometric consistency over time, due to the lack of explicit 4D modeling. items.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
items.summary: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. We find that much of this gap lies in the harness, which decides what the model sees, what it remembers, and how its outputs become actions over time. items.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
items.summary: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. items.summary: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. items.title: Reading the Unreadable: Text-Aware Image Super-Resolution Needs Reasoning
items.summary: Text-aware image super-resolution (TAISR) aims to recover high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs while preserving textual content. Existing methods treat this as a visual restoration problem, yet severely degraded text often cannot be read from local visual evidence alone. items.summary: Long-horizon, real-time controllable motion generation is essential for interactive animation and humanoid robotics, where an agent must respond to changing instructions and spatial goals while moving. items.summary: Persistent spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents to operate reliably in environments they repeatedly encounter. items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform diverse tasks from visual observations and language instructions. items.summary: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. items.summary: Agentic artificial intelligence could automate analyses of sensitive clinical data, but current agents depend on large language models (LLMs). Cloud LLMs expose patient data.
